roadmap.goal: Slice 04 (ADO Story 5577): a service desk that granted its integration account the `itil` role stops seeing request-to-resolution dressed up as time-in-progress. Lighthouse reads the instance's own state spans, turns them into the moves the record actually made, dates the start of work at the moment someone picked it up — and, where the instance cannot supply that, says so at connection setup instead of quietly shipping the inflated number. Turn the 43 already-authored RED tests green without authoring a single new test.
roadmap.overview: REPLACES SLICE 01's ROADMAP. This file previously held the slice-01 (Story #5574) plan; that version is preserved in git history at commit d7401b80b and is not reproduced here. Step ids are namespaced `04-NN` so they never collide with slice 01's `01-NN` in the shared execution log. UNUSUAL SHAPE, inherited from slice 01 — DISTILL has already written every acceptance test AND every production scaffold. This roadmap plans NO test authoring. It plans turning 38 backend RED + 5 frontend RED tests green, in the order the data flow implies, and deleting the scaffolds that made them RED. Backbone: 04-01 the query core (what is asked of the instance, what is kept of the answer, 12 tests) -> 04-02 the span mapper (spans become moves; when work started, 10 tests) -> 04-03 the capability verdict and its advisory copy (9 tests) -> 04-04 the connector composes the history read (5 tests) -> 04-05 StartedDate moves onto the first Doing span (1 test) -> 04-06 ValidateConnection carries the advisory (0 tests, and that is exactly why it gets its own step) -> 04-07 the frontend reads the validation answer (5 tests) -> 04-08 the frontend service stops collapsing that answer to a boolean (0 tests) -> 04-09 the wizard and the settings page actually show the advisory (0 tests, THE EXIT GATE) -> 04-10 the walking skeleton through the real ASP.NET host (1 test). RED mechanism is NOT the project's usual RED-by-skip and NOT [Ignore]: DISTILL used WRONG-VALUE SCAFFOLDS — `__scaffold__` sentinels, `DateTime.UnixEpoch`, an 8000-character string, a conservative `NoStateMetric` constant — so every test already fails at its assertion site with a real NUnit or Vitest failure and the expected/actual diff reads as the specification. Nothing is skipped, `dotnet build` is clean at zero warnings and `pnpm build` is clean. Each step replaces one scaffold body and removes that file's `// SCAFFOLD (DISTILL slice 04, Story #5577)` marker and its sentinel constants as part of the step, so the DoD sweep is distributed rather than deferred to a cleanup pass. THREE STEPS TURN ZERO RED TESTS GREEN (04-06, 04-08, 04-09) and are load-bearing anyway: they are the advisory's path from the connector to the administrator's screen. DISTILL specified that path and authored the pure function at each end, but authored nothing over the wiring between them. If those three ship undone the slice produces an advisory nobody ever reads, and ADR-117's honesty obligation — the reason this slice exists — is unmet.

locked_decisions.adr_118_1: Transitions are derived at each span's `start`, never from `end` or `duration`. 128 of 189 rows on the PDI carry an empty `end`, so open spans need no special case, and the Glide epoch-offset duration is never parsed.
locked_decisions.adr_118_2: Spans are filtered by metric DEFINITION — `metric_definition` on the configured table with `type = Field value duration` — not by field name and not by field emptiness. Filtering on the `field` name was rejected: it hardcodes which field counts as state per table and is blind to a customer's own definitions.
locked_decisions.adr_118_3: `metric_instance.value` is the LABEL; `field_value` is the choice number and is never read. No choice-label resolver is built anywhere.
locked_decisions.adr_118_4: Chunk at 200 sys_ids. The measured 8192-byte URL cliff sits between 245 ids (8182 bytes, 200 OK) and 250 (8347 bytes, 414). A 414 is loud, which is the point: an over-long batch cannot silently return partial history.
locked_decisions.adr_118_5: The capability disclosure lives in `ValidateConnection` only. It is not persisted and it MUST NOT reach the metrics UI.
locked_decisions.adr_118_6: AC5's opt-in team setting is NOT built. Measured cost is ~2.4 s per 500 items.
locked_decisions.adr_118_7: `StartedDate` switches to the first Doing span's `start` where history is readable, and falls back to ADR-117's `opened_at` where it is not. `ClosedDate` does NOT switch — `resolved_at` is a genuine recorded instant, unlike the absent `work_start` that forced `StartedDate` to substitute in the first place.

phases.name: Time-in-state on ServiceNow work comes from the instance's own history
phases.description: Turn 43 already-authored RED tests green: the three pure cores, the connector's composition of them, the start-of-work switch, and the advisory's path from the connector through the validation response to the administrator's screen — plus the walking skeleton through the real ASP.NET host.

steps.name: What is asked of the instance, and what is kept of the answer
criteria: A team's records are split into batches no larger than the measured safe size, every record appears exactly once across the batches, and a team that fits in one batch is not split
A team whose query matched nothing asks for nothing — no batch, and therefore no request that would read every span in the instance

A full batch's assembled query stays comfortably under the measured URL cliff, with room left for the instance address, the path and the other request parameters. This is the single check standing between a full batch and a 414 that fails the whole sync

The definition query names the configured table and the kind of measurement that records how long a field held each of its values — script-calculation definitions share the field with the real spans, so the kind is the discriminator, not the field name

The span query restricts to BOTH the records asked about and the definitions that actually measure state: without the record filter it reads every span in the instance, without the definition filter it reads rows that are not spans at all
A span row is read for its state label, never for its choice number — the number means different states on different tables, so mapping by it would be wrong on every table but one
Rows produced by a definition that does not measure state are discarded. Keeping them fabricates state changes out of assignment changes and script calculations
A span's start is read in universal time. The instance-local form of the same instant falls on the previous calendar day in the fixture, and everything downstream buckets by day
A row whose start cannot be read is not a span at all — no epoch, no now, no substitute instant. A fabricated instant in a state-time chart reads as measurement
An empty answer produces no spans
All 12 cases in ServiceNowHistoryQueryTest green (12 of the 43); the SCAFFOLD marker and the `__scaffold__` sentinel constant gone from this file; `dotnet build` zero warnings
ALREADY GREEN, MUST STAY GREEN: the three ServiceNowHistoryPurityArchUnitTest cases — this core must not acquire an HttpClient, a logger or a persistence dependency while it grows a body
steps.scenario_name: A full batch's query stays under the measured URL limit, and only rows from a definition that measures state survive as spans
steps.implementation_notes: FIRST because it sits at the head of the data flow — rows become spans here, and 04-02 consumes what this produces. 12 of the 43 in one step. FINDING THAT WILL BITE IMMEDIATELY: the Reuse Analysis (feature-delta.md L2108) says to REUSE ServiceNowWorkItemMapper's tolerant two-form field read, but that reader and both form constants (UniversalForm = "value", ReadableForm = "display_value") are PRIVATE. Widening them to `internal` is the smallest honest move and keeps one tolerant reader for the whole connector; duplicating the null / absent / bare-scalar tolerance into this file is the alternative and is worse, because that tolerance is exactly what the metric rows need and a second copy will drift. Decide once, here, and note it in the commit body. FIELD MAPPING for a span row, following the mapper's existing split (identifiers and instants from the universal form, human-facing labels from the readable form): RecordId <- `id`.value; Label <- `value`.display_value; Start <- `start`.value parsed with `AdjustToUniversal | AssumeUniversal` and `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` (Bug #5567 is the ledger entry for what relabelling costs — never `SpecifyKind`). THE URL BUDGET IS TIGHT: 200 ids x 32 hex chars + 199 separators is ~6599 characters before the definition clause, and the test bounds the result at 7000 — so this function must NOT URL-encode; encoding happens where the URI is built, in 04-04. `RecordsPerBatch` (200) and `StateSpanDefinitionType` ("Field value duration") are already public consts and the tests read them, so do not rename or inline them. LIVE-INSTANCE RISK worth naming in the commit body: the definition query filters on the literal `Field value duration`, which is the choice LABEL; a real instance may need the underlying value (`field_value_duration`) in `sysparm_query`. The test pins the label because ADR-118 states it that way; the dogfood moment is what proves it, and it is the first thing to check if the PDI returns zero definitions. CI ledger rules that bite here: NUnit2046 / NUnit4002 / CA1861 are pre-commit HARD BLOCKS if you touch the test file (do not); CA1859 — every new private helper takes and returns the CONCRETE `List<T>` / `string[]`, never an interface, and the rule applies to parameters too; SYSLIB1045 — no `new Regex(...)`, this is string building; CA1869 — if any `JsonSerializerOptions` appears, cache it in a `static readonly` field; S2325 / S1144 — a private helper that touches no instance state must BE static (this is a static class, so all of them are); S8969 / S8970 — zero null-forgiving `!` anywhere, ERROR severity since SonarAnalyzer.CSharp 10.30 and it breaks the build, not just the gate; S3776 — keep the row reader under cognitive complexity 15, extract before adding a third branch.

steps.name: Spans become the moves between them, and the moment work actually started
criteria: Three spans describe two moves: consecutive spans pair into `previous label -> current label`, and each move is dated by the ARRIVAL — the start of the span being entered, never the end of the one being left. The two differ by roughly thirty seconds on a live instance whenever the metric calculation lags
Spans that arrive out of order are paired by when they started, not by the order the Table API happened to return them in. Pairing unsorted spans produces moves that never happened

The earliest span is an arrival nobody witnessed and is not reported as a move. Spans begin only when the metric definition was activated, so a record older than that has a first observed label that is not necessarily the state it was created in — manufacturing a move into it would assert a state the record may never have held

A reopened record reports the journey back out of Done: a later span carrying an already-held label pairs into a move from Done back into Doing, which is exactly what a flow coach investigating rework needs to see

Two labels the team has grouped under one state produce no move between them — the team called them one state because it considers them one state, and reporting churn between them would put phantom transitions in every state-time chart
A record with no history reports no moves

Work started when the record first reached a state the team calls Doing. Nine days sitting in the queue is queue time, and counting it as work is precisely what ADR-117 accepted only until this slice existed
Work that returned to Doing started the FIRST time it got there — rework must not restart the clock, or Cycle Time reports a fraction of the work's life as though the first attempt never happened

Work that never left the queue has not started, and neither does a record with no spans at all. Saying otherwise would put every untouched ticket into Cycle Time and Work Item Age with a start date it never earned
All 10 cases in ServiceNowStateSpanMapperTest green (10 of the 43); the SCAFFOLD marker and the `__scaffold__` sentinel constant gone from this file; `dotnet build` zero warnings
ALREADY GREEN, MUST STAY GREEN: the three ServiceNowHistoryPurityArchUnitTest cases
steps.scenario_name: Consecutive spans become the moves between them, dated by the arrival — and work started the first time the record reached a state the team calls Doing
steps.implementation_notes: The headline behaviour of the slice, and where the mutants will land alongside 04-01. AC2 REQUIRES THE SHARED PATH: build raw transitions (`previous.Label -> current.Label` at `current.Start`) and then hand them to `WorkItemStateTransitionMapper.MapToMappedStates(raw, owner)` UNCHANGED — that shared mapper is what maps raw labels to the team's mapped names and drops self-transitions, which is the only reason `TwoLabelsTheTeamTreatsAsOneState_ProduceNoMoveBetweenThem` collapses three spans to one move with FromState "Working". Do not reimplement either behaviour locally; the whole point of ADR-118's label finding is that ServiceNow needs no mapping surface of its own. Sort by `Start` FIRST, then pair — `SpansArrivingOutOfOrder_ArePairedByWhenTheyStarted` is the only thing standing between a stable sort and invented moves, and the Table API promises no order. `WhenWorkStarted` is the earliest span by `Start` whose label the owner maps to the Doing category, or null — note the two null cases are different questions (never reached Doing / no spans at all) that both arrive here as nothing to report; the caller decides which it is, this function only reports what the spans support. Both public signatures already exist and every test is written against them — `ToTransitions(IReadOnlyList<ServiceNowStateSpan>, IWorkItemQueryOwner)` and `WhenWorkStarted(...)` — so do not change them. `ServiceNowStateSpan` carries RecordId, Label and Start and DELIBERATELY carries no End and no Duration (ADR-118 D6 made structural); do not add them for convenience, the ArchUnit fixture's own comment records why. CI ledger rules that bite here: CA1859 on any new private helper (concrete `List<T>` in and out, parameters included); S2325 / S1144 — static class, so every helper is static and must justify its existence; S8969 / S8970 — zero `!`; S3776 — the pairing loop plus the sort plus the mapper call is already three concerns, extract before adding a fourth. Sonar only re-scans PRs and the Nightly, so a clean local build here proves nothing about the gate.

steps.name: Two different reasons the history is missing, and two different remedies
criteria: An instance that measures state spans on the configured table can supply history
An account the instance refuses the metric tables to lacks the rights — the measured signal is a refusal for every read-only role, opening only at `itil` grade

A refused read that returned nothing is about rights, not about configuration. Both cases saw zero definitions; only one of them is a permissions problem, and telling an administrator to go configure a metric they cannot even see sends them after entirely the wrong thing

An answer nobody expected is not treated as working. Assuming availability from an unrecognised response would have the connector ask for spans it cannot get and report an empty history as though it were a record that never moved

A missing capability does not fail the connection. The advisory rides a success — ServiceNow without `itil` still gives a team its throughput and its forecast, and failing validation would stop an administrator finishing a setup that works

An instance that can supply history carries no advisory at all — neither the text nor its code. Nothing to warn about, so nothing is said, and an empty banner in front of an administrator with nothing to act on is worse than silence
The advisory for missing rights names the role to grant. An administrator cannot act on 'history unavailable'; they can act on the name of a role
The advisory for a missing metric names the configured table and the kind of measurement to activate. Naming the metric kind is what turns a complaint into an instruction

Whichever cause fired, the advisory says which number the team is actually going to get — that the measurement is request-to-resolution rather than time in progress. Shipping the inflated number unqualified is what this slice exists to stop, and it is ADR-117's honesty obligation coming due

All 11 cases in ServiceNowHistoryVerdictTest green — 9 of the 43 newly green, plus the 2 argued greens that must not regress; the SCAFFOLD marker and the `__scaffold__` sentinel constant gone from this file; `dotnet build` zero warnings

ALREADY GREEN, MUST STAY GREEN: `AnInstanceMeasuringNothing_HasNoStateMetric` (the conservative constant matched its own case) and `AnAnswerNobodyExpected_IsNotTreatedAsWorking` (a negative assertion any conservative value satisfied) — both become load-bearing the moment the verdict has a body, and the three ServiceNowHistoryPurityArchUnitTest cases
steps.scenario_name: An account that is refused the metric tables is told to grant a role; an instance measuring nothing is told to activate a measurement — and neither one fails the connection
steps.implementation_notes: Independent of 04-01 and 04-02 — it could run first, and is placed third only so the two cores that feed the connector land together. The rung order is a refusal outranking the count: a refusal is NoRights whatever the definition count says, then a successful read with at least one matching definition is Available, then a successful read with none is NoStateMetric. OPEN DECISION THE TESTS DO NOT CONSTRAIN, and the one thing to record in the commit body rather than decide silently: an UNRECOGNISED status (the fixture uses 500) is pinned only by a negative assertion — it must not be Available, and the enum offers no third non-available value that is honest about it. NoRights would tell an administrator to buy a role that changes nothing; NoStateMetric would send them to activate a definition that already exists. Both remedies are wrong for a 500. Pick the one you can defend, write down why, and note that this is the rung neither the SPIKE nor the tests measured — the same provenance problem slice 01 marked with its `Hypothesis_` prefix. `NoRightsCode` and `NoStateMetricCode` already exist as public consts and the tests read them; `ConnectionValidationResult.SuccessWith(code, advisory)` already exists and is the factory for the two advisory cases, with plain `Success()` for Available. ADVISORY COPY IS USER-VISIBLE TEXT and the mutation ledger's single most common survivor is a test that compares a value to the constant it came from — the tests pin the LITERALS "itil", "Field value duration", the table name and "resolution" (case-insensitive), so blanking the copy to "" is caught. Write the copy so each of those literals earns its place in a sentence an administrator can act on, not as a keyword list assembled to satisfy the assertions. The table name goes into the message by string interpolation; SYSLIB1045 forbids `new Regex(...)` and nothing here needs one. Other CI ledger rules: CA1859 on private helpers (concrete types, parameters included); S2325 / S1144 — static class; S8969 / S8970 — zero `!`; S1192 territory if the same literal appears three times, hoist it to a private const. This core must stay pure — the ArchUnit fixture forbids it acquiring a logger, and its own `.Because` clause says why: what an administrator needs to know about a missing capability belongs in the advisory they read, not in a log line nobody opens.

steps.name: The connector reads the history: the measurement first, then the spans, in one batched call
criteria: An instance that measures state spans is DECLARED to supply history — the connector stops answering from a constant and starts answering from what the instance actually said. This is AC1 and the whole point of the slice

The state measurement is resolved BEFORE the spans are asked for. Without that read there is nothing to restrict the span request to, and an unrestricted span read is how assignment changes become state transitions

Every record's history is asked for at once rather than one record at a time: two records fit in one batch, so exactly one span request is made, and it carries the batch as a list of record handles. At roughly 600 ms per call with no rate limiting the constraint is wall clock — one call per work item would turn a 500-item sync into five minutes
Work synced with history carries the moves it made. The pure mapper being right is worth nothing if the connector never hangs the transitions on the work items

An instance that refuses the metric tables downgrades rather than failing: the team's work still syncs, only the history is missing, and the connector declares history unsupported so the existing sync-delta derivation takes over. This is AC4 and it is what a customer sees when the role is revoked after a connection validated perfectly well
An instance that is readable but measures no state spans downgrades the same way, and must not be reported as the rights case

Downgrading says so rather than going quiet. A team quietly losing time-in-state reads as a team whose work never moves, and the administrator has no way to discover why — DoD 5 forbids the silent no-op
A team whose query matched nothing asks for no history at all. An unfiltered request for record handles is an unfiltered read of every span in the instance

All 10 cases in ServiceNowTransitionHistoryTest green except the start-of-work case, which is 04-05 — 5 of the 43 newly green here; both SCAFFOLD markers in the connector's capability field and read seam gone; `dotnet build` zero warnings

ALREADY GREEN, MUST STAY GREEN — check these explicitly, not only at the end: `AnInstanceThatRefusesTheMetricTables_DowngradesRatherThanFailing` and `AnInstanceMeasuringNoStateSpans_DowngradesRatherThanFailing` are regression guards proving read-only customers keep the fallback, and `ATeamWithNoWork_AsksForNoHistoryAtAll` stops being vacuous the moment a history read exists. The four pre-existing ServiceNowTeamSyncAcceptanceTest scenarios must also stay green — the local listener has the state-span measurement OFF by default precisely so they do
steps.scenario_name: The connector resolves the state measurement, asks for every record's spans in one batched call, and hangs the resulting moves on the work items — or says out loud that it could not
steps.implementation_notes: Where the three cores get composed, and the first step that touches IO. The seam is already marked at ~L144 of GetWorkItemsForTeam, immediately after the paged record read, and the capability field plus SupportsTransitionHistory are marked at ~L73-90. That field starts as 'not observed' rather than Linear's optimistic default ON PURPOSE — claiming a capability nobody has checked is the shape of failure this epic exists to prevent — so it turns Available only after a definition read actually succeeded. SHAPE: read `metric_definition` once with the definition query, take the status AND the count of matching rows into the verdict, store the verdict, and branch. On Available, batch the record handles, issue one read per batch, filter the rows to the state-span definitions, group the spans by record, map each record's spans to transitions and set them on the mapped item BEFORE it becomes a `WorkItem` — the copy constructor preserves SyncedTransitions and `WorkItemTest.Construct_FromWorkItemBaseCarryingSyncedTransitions_PreservesTransitions` is the green test that proves it, but this project has been bitten before by `[NotMapped]` init-only properties the copy constructor drops, so verify rather than assume. On anything else, log ONE warning naming the team and the reason, skip the span read entirely, and leave the transitions empty so WorkItemService's sync-delta branch runs. EXTEND the existing paged reader, do NOT fork it — the history reads are the same Table API with the same paging semantics, and chunking by record handle is a caller concern layered on top rather than a second pager. It currently ignores non-OK statuses; the verdict needs the status, so widen what it returns rather than adding a parallel reader. NO NEW IO ABSTRACTION: `ServiceNowHistoryQuery` is pure and the connector owns the HTTP — that is why DESIGN's `ServiceNowHistoryReader` was renamed, and inventing a reader now breaks ADR-114's shell/core split and the ArchUnit fixture with it. The connector is already 690 lines and one parameter under the S107 ceiling, so extract the history read into private methods rather than growing GetWorkItemsForTeam, which is already at three concerns against a cognitive-complexity bound of 15. risks.risk: A record whose history IS readable but which never reached a state the team calls Doing is covered by no connector-level test. A crafter who leaves the request-logged fallback in place for that case will be green and inconsistent with the pure core, which says explicitly that nothing means not started.
risks.mitigation: Stated as a criterion in 04-05 with the distinction spelled out — 'no spans at all' keeps the fallback (mixed provenance, accepted in ADR-118), 'spans but none Doing' does not — and the choice goes in the commit body.

risks.risk: ValidateConnection gains a second round trip, and 04-04 widens the paged reader to surface non-OK statuses. Both touch code paths that four connectors' worth of shipped behaviour flows through, and slice 01's closed-port walking skeleton is the only test that exercises the real transport path.
risks.mitigation: The capability read sits strictly after the existing probe's early returns, so every failure rung short-circuits before it; the whole ServiceNowConnectionAcceptanceTest fixture is 04-06's regression suite. If the paged reader's return shape changes, re-run the slice 01 and slice 02 ServiceNow fixtures before moving on, not at the end.

risks.risk: The advisory must not reach the metrics UI (D-04-3). This is structurally satisfied rather than tested — no metrics component receives a ConnectionValidationResult — so nothing stops a future step from opening that path, and nothing would catch it.
risks.mitigation: Carried as a criterion in both 04-06 and 04-09 and named as a reviewer item in validation.notes. DISTILL considered and rejected a test asserting an absence across the whole UI, which would be brittle and would still not cover a component added later.

risks.risk: No DEVOPS wave has ever run for this epic. The DESIGN wave's Pact recommendation for the metric_definition and metric_instance response shapes is unrouted, so nothing outside the dogfood moment will notice if ServiceNow changes either table's contract.
risks.mitigation: Recorded, not blocking for slice 04 — no live-instance test is authored, so no runner credential or CI path-scope input is needed. Route the contract-test recommendation when DEVOPS runs; it has now been carried across three slices.
